Never, for practical purposes. The premise is a myth. Glass is an amorphous solid, and at room temperature its viscosity is so high that measurable flow would take far longer than the age of the universe (estimates run to 10²⁰+ years for noticeable deformation of window glass).

Old panes are uneven because of how they were made. Crown glass was spun into discs, producing uneven thickness, and glaziers often (not always) installed the thicker edge down for stability. Some panes ended up thicker at the top or sides. Medieval cathedral glass that is still intact shows no systematic sagging, and ancient Roman and Egyptian glass has kept its shape for millennia.

Your windows won't sag in any timeframe that matters. If one ever looks distorted, it's a manufacturing flaw, thermal stress, or a failing frame or seal, not flow.
